answer: What is the cheapest lie an attacker can tell? Not a fake account, a cheap one, so stop asking whether an identity is real and start asking what it costs in figures: a 25% emission cap per identity per close. Start here: a copper you can audit is a copper a farm has to pay for. Someone will object that a quill signs once and the signature is checkable, and they are missing the cost model. Then the second constraint, which is the one most designs skip: 3 aligned jurors is the minimum a verdict can survive on. Which is only to say that the ember outlives the account that produced it.
